bodyText:
LOOKING GLASS · GATE 12 · PUBLIC FICTIONAL BENCHMARK
Coordinate without erasing disagreement
PASS within the declared software scope

The procedure selected P2 while Archive still recommended P3 and Dispatch still recommended P1. Both local references, judgments and their provenance remained inspectable.

No humans participated and no action was enacted. This tests software preservation, not human coordination, consent, fairness or a visual advantage.

Open paused instrument
All 13 preserved replays
Primary-source review

A joint choice can retain different judgments

The three fictional modes expose the same public facts to both groups. Archive ranks retained channels; Dispatch ranks speed. Rank zero is first. The declared procedure minimizes the worse ordinal rank among eligible modes, breaking ties in P1 → P2 → P3 order.

BASE assignment, all modes eligible
Mode	Channels / minutes	Archive rank	Dispatch rank	Worse rank
P1	2 / 1	2	0	2
P2 selected	4 / 3	1	1	1
P3	6 / 5	0	2	2

Both local recommendations are correct for their declared objectives. The procedure is stipulated; its result makes no claim about fairness, utility or agreement.

Untouched 1280 × 720 original. P2 matches neither first choice; the P3/P1 recommendations remain visible.
Negative and sensitivity controls
Expected	Observed	Meaning and limit
Missing proposal: no action	Actual first use records Archive, then a blocked evaluation before Dispatch.	A procedural prerequisite; no inferred human approval.
Only P1/P3 eligible: tie	P1 selected by fixed order; P3/P1 judgments retained.	The tie-break is explicit, not a consensus rule.
No eligible modes: no action	Both proposals persist beside the blocked outcome.	Disagreement is retained even without a joint choice.
Change Dispatch to the detail reference	Fresh branch selects P3; the old branch remains P3/P1.	Reference sensitivity, not evidence of persuasion or consent.
Untouched 960 × 720 original. NONE produces no action while both recommendations remain.
Untouched 960 × 720 original. The new reference-control branch has two distinct group records, even with the same modeled first choice.
What the browser evidence establishes

Candidate 002 completed 79 successful host actions and 93 complete observations. All semantic fingerprints, information hashes, viewport fields and scene measurements match their captures. Two diagram/plain information pairs and all 18 paused checkpoint comparisons match. The first document retains two local branches, four immutable proposals, five created outcomes and three reused evaluations.

Untouched 1279 × 904 original. The plain representation preserves the same substantive information; no visual advantage was measured.

The independent audit passed 73 focused checks, rehashed 102 closed-core files and verified 1,613 earlier frozen entries unchanged. Exports contain their own event: 54 events in the first document and 18 in the reloaded document. A new document UUID separates provenance from semantic state. Local history is held in document memory; export it before reload.

Candidate 001 remains a failure with 43 observations, 31 action attempts (29 completed, two failed) and six originals. Its retained-record Inspect control stayed disabled, its branch registry duplicated a local entry, and a source hash crossed a card boundary. The failed Inspect attempt and a separate host locator error are included in that count. One justified revision corrected the application defects; candidate 002 then passed actual retained-record inspection. The earlier numeric checks did not substitute for that browser result.

Coverage limits. Active tour captures occurred near 0, 9.522 and 20.242 seconds. No separate active frames cover 4–8, 12–16 or 16–20 seconds; event records and paused checkpoints support those boundaries. This is not continuous visual observation. The raw public canonical registry preloads scripted records; the active display and event origins distinguish playback from local actions.

Explicit 1280 × 720 and 960 × 720 layouts passed; a default 1279 × 904 viewport was also recorded, and the override was reset. Lower controls and JSON panels require scrolling. Reduced-motion emulation was not tested. The closed-core audit precedes this results page's separate presentation and route review.

Watch the saved 24-second tour

Open the instrument, choose Reopen saved start, then Play. Archive is recorded at 4 seconds, Dispatch at 8, P2 is selected at 12, the plain view appears at 16, and the P1 tie-break appears at 20. At 24 the opening display is restored and the tour stops. The actual natural run took 24.002 seconds and recorded all eight scripted/automatic events.

For local inspection, create a new branch, record the proposals and evaluate. Inspect retained outcomes to compare their recorded contexts. The DETAIL_CONTROL assignment starts a fresh branch; it does not rewrite the first one.

Exact local restart
Source-informed, with a narrow claim

Star and Griesemer (1989) and Schmidt and Bannon (1992) motivate preserving local viewpoints and inspectable coordination records. Dahleh and colleagues provide adjacent formal context about local information and strategic equilibria. This fixture instead uses common public facts with different objectives. None of these sources establishes human benefit from this instrument. See the bounded primary-source review.

Actual roles: GPT-6 Astra xhigh specification/synthesis; GPT-5.6 Luna high sources; GPT-5.6 Sol high implementation and a separate Sol high audit worker. The host handled supported browser controls and evidence preservation. These are software-agent roles.

Next decision

Approve Gate 13 — A persuasive but wrong view?

Gate 13 remains unapproved and unrun. No human study follows from this software result. Gates 0–11 remain preserved, including Gate 10's negative prediction-workflow result.

Gate 12 · Closed-core verdict: PASS_DECLARED_SOFTWARE_SCOPE. This synthesis precedes final presentation review, complete gate freeze and Git publication.
